hero.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in fiery head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
hero.body:
A 40-year-old man died Sunday morning following a head-on collision on State Road 710 in Martin County, the Florida Highway Patrol reported. The crash took place around 2 a.m. near the intersection of State Road 710, commonly called Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane.

According to FHP investigators, a 2015 Kia Optima traveling northbound on SR-710 drifted across the center line into the southbound lane. The vehicle then struck a 2021 Toyota Tundra head-on, with the left front of the Kia colliding with the left front of the truck. The impact caused the Kia to ignite immediately. The sedan came to rest on the grass shoulder facing north after the crash, while the Tundra remained in the southbound lane, positioned facing southeast.

The Kia driver, the 40-year-old man, was pronounced dead at the scene. The truck's driver, a 41-year-old Indiantown resident, was airlifted by Lifestar helicopter to a hospital for treatment of injuries sustained in the collision. The identities of both drivers have not been released by authorities.

The Florida Highway Patrol continues to investigate the circumstances surrounding the crash. The agency has not disclosed details about what may have caused the Kia to cross into the opposing lane.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins' wife of running anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.body:
Several X accounts were shut down after prominent members of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team alleged that Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins, had been operating them anonymously. Christina Pushaw, a Communications Specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both conducted online research connecting the accounts to the Second Lady. The two accounts in question were @FSUdude01670 and @bobnamy1.

The allegations center on evidence linking the accounts to Layla Collins' contact information. Robert Salvador, CEO of Promota, shared research showing that @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email similar to ones known to be associated with Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying the connection through two-factor authentication records. The screenshots showed that access attempts to the account triggered messages sent to an email address with most letters hidden and to a phone number displaying only the final digits. Redfern stated plainly that the FSUDude account was directly tied to her personal cell phone number.

Pushaw analyzed the content of these accounts to strengthen the case against Collins. She noted that the account's posts fell into two distinct categories: promoting Jay Collins and attacking individuals who refused to endorse him, including the Governor himself. "A regular supporter of Jay Collins is probably not going to be talking trash about the governor like that," Pushaw posted. She also questioned whether someone serving on an important state board, particularly one appointed by DeSantis, would have time to consistently maintain and post from burner accounts. Pushaw pointed out that Collins was appointed by the same governor whose administration she was now criticizing.

Both accounts were deactivated shortly after Pushaw and Redfern publicly raised their concerns. Florida Politics requested comment from both Jay and Layla Collins but had not yet received a response at the time of reporting. Both Pushaw and Redfern have previous experience in DeSantis' communications office, having previously served as Press Secretary. Redfern currently works for Attorney General Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year. The timing of the account deactivations after the public accusations suggests the allegations may have prompted action from Collins or her representatives.

cards.headline: Florida Secretary of State seeks to bar Rep. Paula Stark from ballot over missing financial disclosure
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking a Leon Circuit Court to keep Rep. Paula Stark off the ballot after the St. Cloud Republican failed to properly submit required financial disclosure paperwork before the qualifying deadline.
cards.body:
Florida Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking the court to keep Rep. Paula Stark off the ballot, disputing her account of a paperwork mix-up that left her disqualified from the race. Five state employees submitted sworn written declarations saying Stark's Treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests, and was not accidentally handed it back when he submitted other paperwork in the final hour of the qualifying window on June 12. Stark's incomplete qualifying materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline.

Byrd argued that if Stark or Davis had questioned why the Form 6 was allegedly handed back, the mistake would have been discovered while Davis was at the Division. Election Records Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve said in a court declaration that three weeks after the deadline passed, Stark still has not submitted a Form 6. Reeve noted Stark was one of 12 candidates who did not properly turn in the form, though half of them corrected the problems and still qualified. Reeve also detailed issues with Davis's filings, including a campaign finance report filed over one month late, reported excessive contributions, and an incorrect address on file. Audits found inconsistent amounts transferred between campaign and office accounts in 2022 and 2024.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida students reach historic milestone with 60% scoring at grade level in reading and math
cards.teaser: For the first time in state history, 60% of Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math on the annual FAST exam, marking a significant increase from just three years ago.
cards.body:
Florida students achieved a historic milestone with 60% of students testing at or above grade level in both reading and math on the annual Florida Assessment of Student Thinking (FAST) exam. This marks the first time in state history that the state has reached this threshold for combined reading and math proficiency on the standardized assessment. Just three years ago, roughly half of Florida students read at grade level, representing a meaningful climb in student performance statewide.

The improvement extended to school grade distributions as well. This year, 76% of Florida's 3,428 graded public schools earned an A or B, up from 71% a year ago. The share of schools earning A grades jumped from 44% to 51%. The achievement was recognized as an honorable mention in the weekly winners category, though the results coincided with legitimate questions about what is driving the improvements.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination with international artists
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation on the historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce offers tours three days a week and hosts an artist-in-residency program attracting creators from around the world.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation, nestled in the historic Crain Estate, is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination by connecting local and international artists. The nonprofit preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who once lived on the property. Mr. Crain, a tile worker by trade, left his mark throughout the facility with craftsmanship visible from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The estate remains largely unchanged from the Crains' time there, preserving original features like the smoking and bourbon room with its man paneling and stained glass.

The property gets its name from the peacocks that have roamed the grounds since the 1970s, when the Crains are believed to have brought in seven birds. Today, over 100 peacocks inhabit the estate, including a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old and known for walking with a limp. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world with simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab, directed by Krystal Masters, offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, including one-on-one instruction for complete beginners in mediums such as sculpting and watercolor.

hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year
hero.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
hero.body:
Families planning Fourth of July celebrations will notice higher prices at the grocery store. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, representing a 4% increase from the previous year. Inflation is the primary driver behind these rising costs, with several key cookout staples experiencing significant price jumps.

The survey reveals which items have become noticeably more expensive. Ground beef prices have increased by 5.5%, while hamburger buns have risen 7.7%. Strawberries have seen the steepest increase at 12.4%, largely due to damage from a Florida frost that affected the harvest. Ice cream prices are also up 5.3%. These items represent some of the most popular choices for Fourth of July menus across the country.

Not all grocery prices have climbed, however. Potato prices have actually decreased this year, offering savings for those planning to serve potato chips or potato salad alongside their grilled items. Corn prices have been more volatile, but locally grown corn from the Glades can provide better pricing options for shoppers. These modest savings can help offset some of the increases seen in other categories.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends several strategies to manage cookout expenses. She emphasizes the importance of shopping strategically by comparing prices across different stores to find the best deals for items on your shopping list. Woroch also highlights that reducing food waste is critical for families looking to keep costs down. The best way to minimize waste begins with careful meal planning before heading to the grocery store. By taking time to plan what you'll actually need and use, families can stretch their cookout budgets further while still enjoying a festive holiday celebration.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie works to expand Midway Road and add Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange at the Florida Turnpike.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council last month approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at the Florida Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in the city.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange for the Turnpike, which is still in the design phase. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters were rescued Wednesday after their small motorized boat sank in the Intracoastal Waterway. Life jackets kept them afloat until help arrived.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community rallies around man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé, Mark. "We received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire," Fenn said.

Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically. So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him," Fenn said. White was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing the piano. She was always the first to lend a hand and loved kids and people. The timing of White's death adds another layer of heartbreak, as her birthday is July 4, just days after she passed away. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago. Her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose to undergo a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. After completing the mastectomy, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for her reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before the procedure was scheduled. According to the denial letter, the surgery involved GalaFlex, a synthetic surgical mesh that the insurer considers investigational with insufficient proof it improves health. While the FDA has approved GalaFlex for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the product's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and believes it is less risky than other options. Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington found a mechanism to make it happen. Anthem stated in response that the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval, though the company said Clark retains the right to appeal. Clark and Billington are continuing to fight the denial.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation that doubles slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation project expected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project, funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees, will nearly double the dock's capacity from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation includes a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades serve a dual purpose: increasing capacity while preventing storm damage during hurricanes and major storms.

During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses that depend on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates passenger boarding from the dock, will be allowed to build a gate at the non-floating section to continue operations. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the dock is central to Stuart's identity and economy. "Stuart is not Stuart without the water," he said. He noted that the current dock becomes congested on busy weekends. Boat captain Parker Fisher, based in Stuart, supports the project. "It's definitely needed some work over the years, so I'm glad they're putting money into it," Fisher said.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: The 44-year-old Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday after injuring her right knee during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week. The 44-year-old posted on Instagram that she is heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles, stating "Coming back to compete again has been a gift, and the opportunity to play alongside (at)venuswilliams once more meant the world to me. I did everything I could but unfortunately my knee just isn't ready to compete." Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday.

Serena's Instagram post included images of four syringes showing the fluid drained from her knee after her singles match, along with a video of her walking with strapping on her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in their first-round doubles match, which was pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. The 46-year-old Venus competed in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could play soon, saying "stay tuned to a city near you."

cards.headline: Argentina survives Cape Verde scare 3-2 in World Cup Round of 16 thriller
cards.teaser: Defending World Cup champion Argentina advanced to face Egypt after beating Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time, with Lionel Messi scoring his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi and Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday and advanced to the World Cup Round of 16 in a thrilling match that went to extra time in South Florida. The go-ahead score for Argentina was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute.

Messi scored in the 29th minute for a 1-0 lead, sneaking behind the Cape Verde defense on a well-timed run as Lisandro Martinez lofted a pass toward him. Messi took a quick touch and hammered a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha for his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal. Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1. Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored equalizers for Cape Verde that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd.

Messi now has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappé in the Golden Boot race as the top scorer. He has 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak and moved two goals ahead of Mbappé on the all-time World Cup list. Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, 40, had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Argentina advanced to face Egypt, which beat Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday, in Atlanta on Tuesday.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is targeting a state championship during the 2026 fall season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and winning the district title. A second-round playoff loss has motivated the program to set higher goals this season. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson highlighted the strength of his senior class, noting that most are four-year seniors who came through the middle school program together. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

To reach the next level, the Scots have intentionally scheduled a more challenging slate of opponents for the fall. Senior Jack Williams explained that the program wants to compete against quality teams to improve and attract new talent. Senior Jack Whelche clarified that the team's primary goal is advancing further in the playoffs than last year, emphasizing that an undefeated regular season means little without postseason success. Senior Edmyer St. Jean noted that summer workouts serve as daily motivation for the team as they prepare to break their previous record when the season begins.

Both Pushaw and Redfern have previous experience in DeSantis' communications office, having previously served as Press Secretary. Redfern currently works for Attorney General Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year. The timing of the account deactivations after the public accusations suggests the allegations may have prompted action from Collins or her representatives.

cards.headline: Florida Secretary of State seeks to bar Rep. Paula Stark from ballot over missing financial disclosure
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking a Leon Circuit Court to keep Rep. Paula Stark off the ballot after the St. Cloud Republican failed to properly submit required financial disclosure paperwork before the qualifying deadline.
cards.body:
Florida Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking the court to keep Rep. Paula Stark off the ballot, disputing her account of a paperwork mix-up that left her disqualified from the race. Five state employees submitted sworn written declarations saying Stark's Treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests, and was not accidentally handed it back when he submitted other paperwork in the final hour of the qualifying window on June 12. Stark's incomplete qualifying materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline.

Byrd argued that if Stark or Davis had questioned why the Form 6 was allegedly handed back, the mistake would have been discovered while Davis was at the Division. Election Records Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve said in a court declaration that three weeks after the deadline passed, Stark still has not submitted a Form 6. Reeve noted Stark was one of 12 candidates who did not properly turn in the form, though half of them corrected the problems and still qualified. Reeve also detailed issues with Davis's filings, including a campaign finance report filed over one month late, reported excessive contributions, and an incorrect address on file. Audits found inconsistent amounts transferred between campaign and office accounts in 2022 and 2024.

cards.headline: Florida students reach historic milestone with 60% scoring at grade level in reading and math
cards.teaser: For the first time in state history, 60% of Florida students tested at or above grade level in both reading and math on the annual FAST exam, marking a significant increase from just three years ago.
cards.body:
Florida students achieved a historic milestone with 60% of students testing at or above grade level in both reading and math on the annual Florida Assessment of Student Thinking (FAST) exam. This marks the first time in state history that the state has reached this threshold for combined reading and math proficiency on the standardized assessment. Just three years ago, roughly half of Florida students read at grade level, representing a meaningful climb in student performance statewide.

The improvement extended to school grade distributions as well. This year, 76% of Florida's 3,428 graded public schools earned an A or B, up from 71% a year ago. The share of schools earning A grades jumped from 44% to 51%. The achievement was recognized as an honorable mention in the weekly winners category, though the results coincided with legitimate questions about what is driving the improvements.

cards.headline: Four Florida municipalities receive $7.2 million in FEMA grants for Hurricane Ian recovery projects
cards.teaser: FloridaCommerce announced $7.2 million in federal grants for Charlotte County, Port of the Islands, Seminole County, and Palatka to fund infrastructure projects and improve storm preparedness nearly four years after Hurricane Ian.
cards.body:
FloridaCommerce announced another round of financial awards through the Hurricane Ian Hazard Mitigation Grant Match Program. The state is distributing $7.2 million in FEMA grants to four municipalities impacted by the Category 4 storm that hit Florida in September 2022. The funds are designed to provide infrastructure recovery while improving emergency preparedness and reducing the impact of future storms.

Charlotte County will receive $5.83 million for a public works hurricane-safe room generator and $93,392 for a leachate waste plant generator project. Port of the Islands Community Improvement District has $750,840 for a Union Road water storage and infrastructure retrofit project. Seminole County received $319,437 for a mitigation reconstruction project on Shad Lane, and the city of Palatka has $283,996 for a lift station generator. The Ian Hazard Mitigation Grant Match Program has already distributed more than $12 million in grants to municipalities. The FEMA funding requires local governments to match the same amount of local money to complete the projects.

cards.headline: U.S. men's soccer team faces Belgium in World Cup knockout round after defeating Bosnia
cards.teaser: The United States men's national team takes the field Monday night against Belgium in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle, having earned the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002.
cards.body:
The United States men's national team will face Belgium on Monday night in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle. The Americans earned the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002, having defeated Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 on Wednesday night. The team played the final 26 minutes plus stoppage time of that match with 10 men after Folarin Balogun was red-carded on what coach Mauricio Pochettino called a maddening call.

Longtime referee Andy Davies told ESPN the contact was purely accidental and an unfortunate result from two players challenging for possession of the ball in a normal football movement. Pochettino said flatly it was never a red card. The American camp noted that Lionel Messi made a nearly identical challenge against Algeria earlier in the tournament and received nothing. Weston McKennie said the decision was bogus. Balogun, one of the team's top players, will watch Monday from the stands. Belgium has won six consecutive meetings against the United States, including a 5-2 friendly rout in March, since the inaugural 1930 World Cup, which remains the lone American victory in the head-to-head. The U.S. won Wednesday without Balogun for the final half-hour. The team is well-coached, physically capable, and playing at a venue where the home crowd will be as loud as any in the tournament.

cards.headline: Americans mark 250th Independence Day with tempered enthusiasm and local focus
cards.teaser: As the United States celebrates its 250th birthday, many Americans interviewed by the Associated Press are tuning out partisan shouting and focusing instead on personal concepts of resilience, local community, and the freedom they enjoy.
cards.body:
Across the United States, many Americans are celebrating their country's 250th birthday by tuning out partisan shouting and social media clamor to focus on their own personal concepts of America the Beautiful. In Associated Press interviews with citizens before the Fourth, auto technician Joe Fuqua-Bejarano in Topeka, Kansas, identified resilience rather than politics as what makes Americans awesome. "We've just all got to find unity somewhere, whether that's in laughter or perseverance, and keep everybody cool," he said from the fireworks stand where he runs a booming side business.

The tempered enthusiasm many Americans expressed contrasts with traditional images of Americans as brash and confident. Christina Zhou, a 25-year-old research assistant from Cambridge, Massachusetts, acknowledged "lots of points of contention going around" but focused on local positive developments. "It feels a little bit more like within our own personal control," she said. In Mont Vernon, New Hampshire, farmer Mindy Dean and her family plan to milk their goats and maybe attend local fireworks, largely unbothered by the 250th celebrations. Conversely, 81-year-old retiree Neil Casey from Nashua, New Hampshire, and his friend Maureen Regan from Cambridge are roaming Boston's historical sites and Fourth of July events, immersing themselves in the anniversary atmosphere.

cards.headline: Thomas Jefferson's contradictory legacy debated as nation marks 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: As the United States celebrates its 250th year, historians say no founder's life and work resonates like Thomas Jefferson's, who embodied both the best and worst of the nation and advanced both sides of issues that have defined the country's path.
cards.body:
As the country's 250th anniversary approaches, historians agree that Thomas Jefferson's life and work resonate unlike any other founder's. According to Jon Meacham, the National Constitution Center's Semiquincentennial Scholar and a prize-winning presidential historian who wrote an entire biography of Jefferson, Jefferson embodied "the very best and the very worst" of the United States. America's founding is rooted in Jefferson's most profound contradiction: the man who proclaimed that "all men are created equal" while remaining a slaveholder to the end of his life. Jefferson advanced and explored both sides of many issues that have defined the country's path, including agrarian self-sufficiency and worldly innovation, pluralism and separatism, and limited government and dreams of an "empire of liberty."

Andrew Burstein, a professor of history at Louisiana State University, describes Jefferson as "no more malleable figure in early America." Historian Peter S. Onuf notes that there have been times in American history when just about everyone would have considered themselves "Jeffersonian," yet even at those moments, Jefferson remained a controversial figure. His legacy is debated even at institutions that owe their existence to him. The University of Virginia, the college he founded and regarded as a signature achievement, features a memorial to thousands of enslaved people who lived and worked there. At Monticello, his mountaintop estate outside Charlottesville, a banner near the entrance displays the Declaration with the caption "After all, our guy wrote it," yet reminders of slavery are pervasive throughout the grounds.

hero.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in fiery head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
hero.body:
A 40-year-old man died Sunday morning following a head-on collision on State Road 710 in Martin County, the Florida Highway Patrol reported. The crash took place around 2 a.m. near the intersection of State Road 710, commonly called Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane.

According to FHP investigators, a 2015 Kia Optima traveling northbound on SR-710 drifted across the center line into the southbound lane. The vehicle then struck a 2021 Toyota Tundra head-on, with the left front of the Kia colliding with the left front of the truck. The impact caused the Kia to ignite immediately. The sedan came to rest on the grass shoulder facing north after the crash, while the Tundra remained in the southbound lane, positioned facing southeast.

The Kia driver, the 40-year-old man, was pronounced dead at the scene. The truck's driver, a 41-year-old Indiantown resident, was airlifted by Lifestar helicopter to a hospital for treatment of injuries sustained in the collision. The identities of both drivers have not been released by authorities.

The Florida Highway Patrol continues to investigate the circumstances surrounding the crash. The agency has not disclosed details about what may have caused the Kia to cross into the opposing lane.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce historic estate into arts destination
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is reshaping Fort Pierce's cultural landscape by operating out of the historic Crain Estate, a property that now serves as both a museum and active arts center. The nonprofit preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, the original owners who filled the estate with their travels and personal touches. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker whose skill is evident throughout the property, with his tilework visible from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The foundation has committed to maintaining the estate's original character rather than commercializing it, keeping approximately 90 percent of the home exactly as it was during the Crains' time there. Visitors can explore the lush gardens and distinctive architecture through guided tours offered every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The couple's extensive travels shaped the estate's unique character and collections. They journeyed around the world nine times, acquiring one-of-a-kind items for their Florida home, including a gazebo shipped directly from India that features small peacock details. The property also showcases the smoking and bourbon room, featuring rich paneling, masculine bathroom colors, and ornate stained glass that opens onto a patio bar. According to art director Krystal Masters, the Crains' worldly acquisitions and personal style created a distinctive home that continues to captivate visitors today.

The property gets its name from the peacocks that have inhabited the grounds for decades. The Crains introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, initially bringing seven birds to the estate. From that original flock, the population has grown to over 100 peacocks. Among them is Bob, a celebrated resident believed to be 60 years old and recognizable by his distinctive limp. Staff hand-feed Bob daily using his own bowls, and the peacocks have become memorable highlights of tours, especially for young visitors who get to feed the birds directly. The Crains' animal collection once extended further, as local lore suggests that Jaxson Crain traveled to South America and returned home with a baby monkey carried in his pocket.

Today, the foundation operates an artist-in-residency program that draws artists from around the world, providing them with simple yet elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab offers accessible classes for both children and adults of all skill levels, with Masters leading one-on-one instruction designed for complete beginners. The lab features diverse mediums including sculpting and watercolor painting. Masters emphasizes that art serves as a therapeutic outlet, allowing students to disconnect from their phones and create something meaningful. She finds fulfillment in watching students leave feeling accomplished and fulfilled, understanding that art provides emotional and creative benefits beyond technical skill development.
